title: Enterprise case studies
intro: Client and enterprise work. Public portfolio case studies — URLs, source, screenshots and internal implementation details are intentionally omitted.

items.name: Sonny's Quivio
items.description: A config-driven, multi-tenant Next.js UI serving 10+ dealer tenants across CRM, SAT and white-label modules, built on a shared library of 30+ reusable components.
items.role: Frontend engineering — multi-tenant UI architecture, component library, performance
highlights: SAT module shipped as an installable PWA with push notifications

sections.p: At a high level, Quivio is an automotive platform whose dealer network needs the same product to present differently per tenant — CRM, SAT and white-label modules across 10+ dealer organisations.
From the frontend perspective, the risk in multi-tenant UI is duplication: a fork per tenant multiplies defects, slows delivery and degrades performance as bundles grow.
bullets: Tenant-specific presentation without tenant-specific codebases
A first paint fast enough for daily operational use
Dashboard analytics and field workflows in one product surface

sections.p: I built the config-driven UI layer and the shared component library the tenant experiences are assembled from, and owned the performance work on it.
bullets: Config-driven composition so tenant differences are data, not branches
A shared library of 30+ reusable components adopted across modules
Performance work on the critical rendering path and bundle graph
The SAT module as an installable PWA with push notifications

sections.p: A conceptual view: tenant configuration resolves at render time into a composition of shared components, with server rendering for the first view and cached, query-managed data for the rest.
bullets: Next.js SSR for first-view rendering
Redux Toolkit for client state; TanStack Query for server state and caching
Recharts for dashboard analytics
Service workers for installability and push notifications

sections.p: Measurement first: Lighthouse in the pipeline, Datadog RUM in the field. The documented results were LCP from 3.8s to 2.6s and a 25% reduction in initial bundle size.
bullets: Code splitting and lazy loading on non-critical modules
Webpack bundle analysis to remove and defer weight
Datadog RUM to confirm improvements against real users

sections.p: 10+ dealer tenants served from one config-driven frontend, a faster first paint, a lighter initial bundle, and an installable SAT experience with push notifications.

items.name: Evaria - Cycles & Wellness
items.description: A WCAG 2.1 AA-compliant React.js patient and admin platform with JWT authentication, role-based access control, real-time data and payment integration.
items.role: Frontend engineering — accessible UI, auth/authorisation surface, API integration
highlights: JWT authentication and role-based access control in the UI
Razorpay payment integration; GraphQL and WebSocket data flows

sections.p: At a high level, two audiences share one platform: patients completing care tasks and administrators managing them. Healthcare context makes accessibility and access control non-negotiable.
From the frontend perspective, the same component set had to serve very different permissions and assistive-technology needs without diverging into two products.
bullets: WCAG 2.1 AA conformance across both surfaces
Role-appropriate UI driven by authorisation, not guesswork
Real-time updates and payments inside an accessible flow

sections.p: I built the accessible React UI for both surfaces and the client-side authentication, authorisation and data-integration layers behind it.
bullets: Accessible component patterns on Material UI and SCSS
JWT authentication handling in the client
Role-based access control shaping navigation and available actions
Razorpay payment integration in the patient flow

sections.p: A conceptual view: an accessible component layer above a data layer that mixes REST and GraphQL requests with a WebSocket channel for live updates, with route and action gating derived from role.
bullets: REST and GraphQL for reads and writes
WebSockets for real-time data flows
Authorisation-aware rendering of navigation and controls

sections.p: Accessibility was tested, not asserted: axe DevTools alongside manual keyboard and screen-reader passes, which brought accessibility defects down by 20%. Security stayed at the boundary: token handling, role gating, and XSS/CSRF-aware data handling.
bullets: Semantic structure, ARIA only where native semantics fell short
Keyboard operability and focus management in dialogs and forms
Contrast and form-error accessibility in clinical contexts

sections.p: An accessible patient and admin platform with 20% fewer accessibility defects, role-appropriate access, real-time data and working payments.

items.name: PVR INOX
items.description: Next.js booking, payment and subscription flows for one of India's largest cinema chains, built on shadcn/ui with 90% statement coverage on booking and payment paths.
items.role: Frontend engineering — transactional flows, state management, test coverage
highlights: 90% statement coverage on booking and payment paths
Booking, payment and subscription flows shipped

sections.p: At a high level, cinema booking is a multi-step transaction at consumer scale: selection, seating, payment, and subscription entitlements, where an abandoned step is lost revenue.
From the frontend perspective, transactional flows fail in the seams — partial state, double submission, interrupted payments. Those are exactly the paths that need the most test pressure.
bullets: Multi-step state that survives navigation and retries
Payment and subscription branches sharing one flow
Confidence to ship changes to revenue-critical screens

sections.p: I shipped the booking, payment and subscription flows and the test suite that protects them.
bullets: Flow composition on shadcn/ui components
Redux Toolkit state for step, selection and transaction status
REST API integration across the transaction steps
Jest and React Testing Library suites on booking and payment paths

sections.p: A conceptual view: a step machine over shared flow state, with UI composed from reusable primitives so payment and subscription variants reuse the same building blocks.
bullets: Single source of truth for flow state
Reusable component primitives over per-screen markup
Error and retry states treated as first-class UI

sections.p: Coverage was concentrated where failure is most expensive: 90% statement coverage on booking and payment paths, with component tests guarding the shared primitives against regressions.
bullets: Behaviour-level tests via React Testing Library
Critical-path coverage over blanket coverage targets
Regression tests accompanying flow changes

sections.p: Booking, payment and subscription flows in production for a national cinema chain, with documented 90% statement coverage on the paths that carry payment.

items.name: UPSC Examination Platform
items.description: The Next.js SSR portal for a high-traffic national examination platform, including the multi-step application form with field-level validation, persisted drafts and secure document upload.
items.role: Frontend engineering — SSR portal, complex forms, performance, accessibility
highlights: Multi-step application form with persisted draft state
Secure photograph, signature and document upload UX

sections.p: At a high level, a national examination portal serves applicants across a wide range of devices, connection quality and languages, in bursts of very high traffic around deadlines.
From the frontend perspective, two problems dominate: keeping pages fast under load, and making a long application form survivable — including uploads that must not be lost.
bullets: Load performance during deadline traffic peaks
A long, validated, resumable application form
Accessibility and multi-locale support as delivery requirements

sections.p: I built the SSR portal and the multi-step application form, and owned the performance and accessibility work on both.
bullets: Server rendering, pagination and caching that cut page load time by 20%
Multi-step form with field-level validation
Persisted draft state so progress is not lost between sessions
Secure photograph, signature and document upload flows

sections.p: A conceptual view: server-rendered routes for first paint, paginated and cached data for list-heavy screens, and a form layer that validates per field and persists progress as the applicant moves through steps.
bullets: Next.js SSR/ISR for render strategy per route
Pagination and caching to bound payload size
Material UI components extended for accessible form patterns
i18n across the applicant-facing surface

sections.p: Government delivery ran through security and accessibility review gates. Uploads needed clear constraints, states and error recovery, and every validation message had to be announced, not just coloured.
bullets: WCAG 2.1 AA structure, labelling and keyboard operability
Field-level errors described programmatically to assistive technology
Explicit upload requirements, progress and failure states

sections.p: A high-traffic national examination portal with 20% faster page loads, a resumable validated application form, and accessible, multi-locale applicant journeys.

items.name: Arab EZ Translator
items.description: The core authoring surface for translation workflows — a rich text editor with formatting controls, live word count and syntax highlighting, built from reusable React components across multiple locales.
items.role: Frontend engineering — editor surface, reusable components, API integration
highlights: Rich text editor with formatting controls and live word count
Reusable React components across multiple locales
Responsive, cross-browser interfaces to WCAG 2.1 AA

sections.p: At a high level, translators work all day in one screen. The authoring surface is the product, so its responsiveness and predictability matter more than anything around it.
From the frontend perspective, a rich text editor concentrates difficulty: formatting state, live feedback and keyboard behaviour all have to stay correct while text is being edited continuously.
bullets: Formatting controls that stay in sync with selection
Live feedback (word count) without interrupting typing
Multi-locale content, including right-to-left considerations

sections.p: I built the authoring surface and the reusable component set behind it, and integrated the REST APIs for content management and translation features.
bullets: Rich text editor with formatting controls
Live word count and syntax highlighting
Reusable React components shared across the product
REST API integration for content and translation workflows

sections.p: A conceptual view: a controlled editor surface with a toolbar driven by current selection state, above a component layer shared with the rest of the application.
bullets: Component composition on Material UI
Locale-aware rendering of the authoring surface
Responsive, cross-browser layout behaviour

sections.p: The interface was built to WCAG 2.1 AA: keyboard-operable formatting controls, labelled toolbar actions, and cross-browser responsive behaviour on real devices.
A reusable, accessible authoring surface for translation workflows across multiple locales and browsers.
